title: Bill Jennings, left-handed guitarist
summary: Thomas describes Jennings learning guitar upside down from his right-handed brother, rumors of his troubles, and urging him to play softer.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You know, Bill Jennings, he was a left-handed guitar player.
And do you know how he learned to play guitar left-handed?

He was left-handed. So his brother played guitar, and his brother was right-handed. So his brother would play something, and then just hand the guitar over to him, and the changes would be upside-down. But he somehow or other learned to play them. His chord formations were a
little different from the average guy. But he learned how to solo on them strings.
I don't know. I heard somebody say that he got his hand cut off. He kept foolin' around with that dope, and I heard... Actually, I never got this confirmed.
Sorry to hear that. I know he was supposed to be driving a cab at one time or something.

He was so great. If I'd have just kept that group together, boy, they could have gone... And one thing I had to tell Bill, I said, "Bill..." He had a problem of playing too loud. I said, "Man, when a man comes in a club with a girl, he wants to be able to talk. And he can't talk if the music is too loud. You've got to play some ballads and things."
